The scheduled worker is the Active Record connection pool reaper, a singleton background thread named "AR Pool Reaper". Its loop calls `pool.reap`, which reclaims connections leased to dead threads, and `pool.flush`, which disconnects connections idle past `idle_timeout`.

`activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/abstract/connection_pool/reaper.rb` is the main implementation: it spawns the thread and runs the periodic maintenance loop.
`activerecord/lib/active_record/connection_adapters/abstract/connection_pool.rb` provides the `reap` (lines 703–721) and `flush` (726+) methods the reaper calls.

The reaper file is the most relevant because it contains the scheduling loop that invokes both methods.

The primitive is `ActiveSupport::Concurrency::ShareLock`, a share/exclusive lock. Many threads hold it shared, one caller can wait for exclusive access, and `yield_shares` lets a thread drop its share temporarily so a pending upgrade can proceed.

The ShareLock class lets an upgrade happen safely: `start_exclusive` (line 75) and `yield_shares` (line 170) release a thread's shared hold when it is compatible with the waiting exclusive request, so two threads both waiting to upgrade cannot block each other.

Mid-job shutdown raises `Continuation::Interrupt`, which `Continuable` catches and turns into a `retry_job` (default `resume_options` wait of 5 seconds). The progress is serialized into the job data under `continuation` and restored by `Continuation.new` on the next run, so completed steps are skipped and the current step resumes from its cursor.
